flags.headline: QCOM down ~11% over 2 sessions (9/18 -5.8%, 9/19 -5.64%) as prior-month rally unwinds
flags.detail: No fresh company-specific catalyst identified today. Coverage frames this as part of a broader semis 'rally unwind' (Skyworks, Qorvo also lower). The move revisits QCOM's already-disclosed Apple in-house-modem risk -- CEO Amon told Reuters after the Q3 FY2026 (7/29/26) earnings call that Qualcomm's iPhone modem share will fall materially below the prior 20% estimate, with Apple-related product revenue down ~50% sequentially into the December quarter -- but that disclosure is ~7 weeks old and already reflected in the stock's ~19% YTD decline, so this is not treated as a new deterioration. Held at AMBER, not escalated to RED, absent new information; watch for a 3rd consecutive down session or fresh Apple-share commentary.
flags.thesis_link: Matches QCOM key_risk: 'Apple modem internalization -- if Apple successfully develops in-house baseband modems, Qualcomm could lose its largest QCT customer (estimated 20-25% of chip revenue)' -- risk already disclosed 7/29/26, not newly materializing today.

evidence.source: Reuters (via multiple outlets citing CEO Amon interview)

flags.headline: STLD -4.18% after Q3 2026 EPS guidance ($5.34-5.38) came in below Street consensus ($5.66)
flags.detail: Steel Dynamics' own 9/17/26 press release guides Q3 profitability meaningfully higher sequentially vs. Q2 (metal-margin expansion, record shipments) but below the higher analyst consensus -- a soft-vs-Street miss, not an absolute guidance cut. Separately, Canada announced 50% retaliatory tariffs on US steel/aluminum, adding a trade-policy overhang. Stock reaction has spread across 9/17-9/19.
flags.thesis_link: Adjacent to STLD key_risk 'steel price cyclicality -- profit margin of 7.22% is thin and earnings can swing 20%+ with steel cycles' -- the guide is a soft version of that swing, not a reversal.
